review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the wordDeriv definition, the commutation and sum lemmas in LocalDivCurlSmooth.lean, and lps_wordDeriv_sub with its private add/mul helpers in SmoothingOrderedProduct.lean. I searched those files and the CKN foundation files for @[simp] attributes and wordDeriv equation lemmas and found none. Many files unfold wordDeriv with `simp [wordDeriv]` (124 occurrences across 37 files by my grep count). I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behavior, such as whether simp loops or what normal form it reaches. I did not recommend making the hypothesis-carrying commutation lemmas simp lemmas. They need smoothness side conditions, and rewriting in the wrong direction could cause trouble. The finding is therefore limited to the missing structural equation lemmas.

findings.problem: `wordDeriv` is a structurally recursive def with no registered equation lemmas such as `wordDeriv_nil` or `wordDeriv_cons`, and no simp attribute on any word-derivative lemma. Callers therefore unfold the definition by hand. Line 58 uses `simpa [wordDeriv]` to turn `wordDeriv [j,j] f` into `spatialDeriv (spatialDeriv f j) j`. This is a whole-definition unfold, so its output depends on simp's reduction of the list literal. Lines 79, 99 and 105 (`change wordDeriv α H x ... = _`) rely on definitional unfolding. Many other files do the same: grep finds 124 `simp ... [wordDeriv` occurrences across 37 files.
findings.proposed_change: In LocalSobolevBall.lean, next to `def wordDeriv`, add two equation lemmas: `@[simp] theorem wordDeriv_nil (f) : wordDeriv [] f = f := rfl`, and `theorem wordDeriv_cons (j α f) : wordDeriv (j :: α) f = wordDeriv α (spatialDeriv f j) := rfl`. Only the nil lemma would be tagged simp. The cons lemma recurses on a strictly shorter list, so it could also be a simp lemma, but whether to tag it is a design choice. Possibly also add `wordDeriv_singleton : wordDeriv [j] f = spatialDeriv f j`. Then line 58 becomes a targeted `simpa only [wordDeriv_cons, wordDeriv_nil]` or `exact`, and the `change` steps can be `rw`/`simp only` with named lemmas. Do not simp-tag the smoothness-conditional commutation lemma `localDivCurlSmooth_wordDeriv_spatialDeriv`.
findings.benefit: The word-derivative simp interface becomes explicit and uniform. Proofs in this file and in the dozens of other `simp [wordDeriv]` callers no longer depend on definitional unfolding or on how simp reduces the definition. The normal form (peel the head letter, then recurse) is documented in the lemma statements.
